summary:
MISSIONFORGE is an interactive space mission design and simulation platform developed to make spacecraft engineering more accessible to students, educators, and space enthusiasts. Inspired by the challenge of designing real-world space missions, it allows users to create mission concepts, assemble spacecraft using different hardware components, select scientific payloads, and configure essential mission parameters.

The platform incorporates first-order engineering analysis to evaluate spacecraft mass, electrical power generation and consumption, battery capacity, orbital characteristics, eclipse duration, and communication and data-handling requirements. Users can examine engineering diagnostics, identify design constraints, and explore their mission through an interactive 3D visualization and simulation environment.

MISSIONFORGE addresses the challenge by transforming complex mission-design concepts into an accessible, hands-on learning experience. It aims to help learners understand how scientific objectives, spacecraft subsystems, and engineering decisions interact when designing a space mission.
details:
MISSIONFORGE is an interactive space mission design and simulation platform that helps students and space enthusiasts explore the engineering behind spacecraft missions. Users can configure a mission, assemble a spacecraft by selecting components, design its electrical subsystem, choose scientific payloads, and examine how engineering decisions affect mission performance.

The platform brings together spacecraft assembly, payload configuration, power-system calculations, orbital analysis, engineering diagnostics, and an interactive 3D Mission Control environment. Its first-order models help users examine parameters such as spacecraft mass, power generation and consumption, battery capacity, orbital period, eclipse duration, and communication and data-handling requirements. Users can identify design constraints, compare subsystem trade-offs, and observe their mission in a visual simulation environment.

Our goal is to make space engineering more accessible, especially to students who may not have access to expensive laboratories or professional mission-design software. By turning complex engineering concepts into an interactive learning experience, MISSIONFORGE encourages experimentation, systems thinking, and interest in space science and technology.

The platform was developed using React, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, React Three Fiber, and Drei, with CSS and JavaScript/TypeScript-based engineering logic. We used NASA and JPL reference resources for selected Earth and orbital parameters. The engineering models are simplified educational approximations, not flight-dynamics certification or mission qualification tools.

The creative aspect of MISSIONFORGE is its integration of spacecraft configuration, subsystem-level engineering analysis, and 3D mission visualization into one learning environment. During development, we considered accessibility, ease of use, engineering plausibility, computational simplicity, affordability, and the importance of showing users how decisions in one spacecraft subsystem can affect the overall mission.
